content.title: What are Custom Exceptions?
content.description: Custom Exceptions are user-defined exception classes created by extending the Exception or RuntimeException class to represent application-specific error conditions.

content.content: Java provides many built-in exceptions, but sometimes applications need to represent domain-specific problems such as an invalid bank transaction, insufficient balance, invalid age, or unauthorized access. In such cases, developers create Custom Exceptions to make error handling more meaningful and easier to understand.

content.title: Why Create Custom Exceptions?
content.content: Custom exceptions make programs easier to maintain by providing meaningful names and messages for application-specific errors.
A custom exception is created by extending either the Exception class (checked exception) or the RuntimeException class (unchecked exception).

content.title: Creating a Checked Custom Exception
Key Idea
content.description: A custom exception behaves like any other Java exception but represents a problem specific to your application.

content.content: Once a custom exception class is created, it can be thrown using the throw keyword whenever a business rule is violated.

content.title: Throwing Custom Exception
Business Rules
content.content: Custom exceptions are commonly used to enforce business rules such as minimum balance, valid user age, or product availability.
Custom exceptions can be handled using the same try-catch mechanism used for built-in Java exceptions.

items.question: Education Systems
items.answer: InvalidMarksException for marks outside the valid range.

content.title: Custom Exception Program

rows: Specific errors are easier to identify.

content.title: School Admission Rules
content.content: A school may reject students who do not meet the minimum age requirement by issuing a special notice. Similarly, a custom exception represents a specific rule violation with a meaningful message.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Java interviews frequently ask candidates to create custom exceptions, explain checked vs unchecked exceptions, and demonstrate when custom exceptions should be preferred over built-in exceptions.

items.question: Should every error have a custom exception?
items.answer: No. Use built-in exceptions whenever they accurately describe the problem.

items.question: Can a custom exception extend RuntimeException?
items.answer: Yes. This creates an unchecked custom exception.

items.question: Should meaningful messages be provided?
items.answer: Yes. Clear exception messages make debugging much easier.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Create custom exceptions when built-in exceptions cannot clearly represent your application's business rules or domain-specific errors.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Use throw to generate custom exceptions.
Handle custom exceptions using try-catch or declare them using throws.
Meaningful exception names improve readability and debugging.
